top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level FPGA wrapper exposing Wishbone-backed firmware-visible MMIO, CPU integration, request/response staging, safety supervision, timeout detection, actuator clamping, heartbeat monitoring, and safe fallback control for active aerodynamics.
top_module.functionality: Integrates a PicoRV32-based control plane with a Wishbone MMIO register file, compact request and response staging, a watchdog and freshness monitor, a safety FSM, and actuator output formatter. Firmware writes request descriptors, updates control and timeout registers, and reads response summaries and status. The hardware independently enforces staleness rejection, timeout handling, clamping, safe fallback, and fault indication. The top-level module does not expose raw tensors, geometry arrays, or flow fields; only compact descriptors and scalar summaries are transported.
responsibilities: Instantiate and connect the CPU, Wishbone interconnect, MMIO register bank, compact request/response staging memories, and safety controller.
Expose a firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with valid/ready semantics, address, write data, read data, and write-enable behavior.
Maintain deterministic safe fallback outputs on reset, timeout, fault, or invalid command conditions.
Clamp actuator outputs independently for positive and negative channels to configured bounds.
Track request and response sequence numbers, freshness, age, and response validity.
Assert irq_o on fault, timeout, stale data, or heartbeat/watchdog events as programmed by firmware policy.
top_module.reset_behavior: On reset deassertion, initialize the safety FSM into SAFE_FALLBACK, clear pending command application, force act_safe high, drive act_valid low, set actuator command outputs to a deterministic low-risk posture, clear transient fault indication only through controlled clear-fault behavior, and hold IRQ low until a fault or watchdog condition is detected after initialization.
behavior_rules: Wishbone accesses shall complete with single-cycle or bounded-latency acknowledge behavior.
The top-level MMIO register map shall be word-addressed and fixed at synthesis time.
Every register described in the register contract shall be directly reachable through RTL decode.
Requests are accepted only through firmware-controlled MMIO writes and are checked for freshness, sequence alignment, and bounds before application.
Responses are rejected if sequence numbers do not match the latest outstanding request or if age exceeds the configured threshold.
If firmware heartbeat is absent beyond the watchdog threshold, the controller must enter safe fallback and assert irq_o.
If clear-fault is asserted while conditions are healthy, the design may transition from FAULT or SAFE_FALLBACK to READY.
No unsynthesizable tasks, delays, or behavioral-only model logic are allowed.
Any bulk history or queue storage shall be implemented via the declared FPGA BRAM macros only.

modules.name: picorv32_wishbone_cpu_subsystem
modules.description: Resolved PicoRV32 soft-CPU subsystem with Wishbone bus master, instruction and data memory integration, UART support, and interrupt input. This block is a system-integration abstraction for the resolved CPU contract and is responsible for firmware execution and MMIO access generation.
modules.functionality: Executes firmware that writes request descriptors, configures safety and clamp registers, polls or responds to interrupts, reads response summaries, and drives actuator update commands through the MMIO map. The subsystem exposes a Wishbone master interface and UART pins per the resolved CPU contract.
responsibilities: Run firmware responsible for command packaging, sequence tracking, status polling, and response validation.
Generate Wishbone accesses to the MMIO/control plane.
Consume irq_i for fault, timeout, stale-data, and watchdog notifications.
Provide UART transmit and receive connectivity for firmware loading and debug in the resolved integration profile.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, halt bus activity, deassert Wishbone strobes, and hold UART/interrupt handling in a reset-safe state until reset_n is released.
behavior_rules: Must treat MMIO as the only control-plane access to the active-aero controller.
Must not assume direct access to model payloads or wide tensors.
Must not bypass firmware-mediated command acceptance or safety validation.
Wishbone master timing must be compatible with a single-clock 50 MHz system.
Interrupts are used for fault and service events, not for streaming inference transport.

modules.name: aero_mmio_register_bank
modules.description: Wishbone-accessible register bank implementing the required firmware-visible control/status contract, including control, status, freshness, timeout, clamp, request descriptor, response summary, and safety-state registers. It decodes all registers and provides explicit semantic outputs and readable status fields.
modules.functionality: Decodes the fixed 32-bit word-addressed register map and presents explicit semantic control outputs to the safety controller while receiving status and response summary inputs for firmware reads. Implements registers for control, status, freshness, timeout, clamp bounds, request descriptors, response summaries, and safe-state programming.
responsibilities: Provide Wishbone register access with bounded-latency acknowledge.
Expose all mandatory firmware-visible registers and fields.
Convert MMIO writes into explicit semantic control outputs.
Collect status and summary inputs for firmware reads.
Drive protected safe-state posture programming fields.
Report register decode errors through wb_err_o when appropriate.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, drive outputs to benign defaults, clear write-side control outputs, and return readable status fields to safe-fallback and fault-cleared baseline values as defined by the safety state machine.
behavior_rules: Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode.
The register bank shall not hide inaccessible internal state as software-visible contract fields.
Semantic outputs are explicit ports and not implicit transport-bus interpretations.
Read data shall reflect current status, freshness, and response summary values with bounded latency.
All register addresses are fixed at synthesis time and word aligned.

modules.name: aero_reqresp_transport_bram
modules.description: Compact request/response staging and history buffer implemented using FPGA-appropriate block RAM. The block stores compact request descriptors, response summaries, and bounded history for sequence traceability and verification without exposing bulk model payloads at the top level.
modules.functionality: Stores compact request descriptors and compact response summaries in BRAM-backed structures, preserving request/response sequence traceability, age tracking, and bounded history for firmware polling and verification. Does not store or expose any wide tensor payloads or flow fields.
responsibilities: Buffer request metadata entries.
Buffer response summary entries.
Expose readable current request and response items for the safety controller and MMIO status logic.
Track current sequence and last-response sequence.
Provide age-counter visibility for freshness checks.
Use only the declared FPGA BRAM macros for storage.
modules.reset_behavior: Clear buffer pointers, valid flags, age counters, and history indices on reset while leaving the underlying block RAM contents unconstrained unless rewritten by the controller.
behavior_rules: The storage implementation shall map to native block RAM in FPGA flow.
No flattened register-array substitute is permitted for bulk request/response storage.
Sequence and age visibility must remain readable for scoreboard-based verification.
BRAM interfaces use explicit control pins; the buffer shall not expose a wide streaming transport to the top level.
req_push and req_pop are control pulses generated internally from request and response staging state, not external top-level inputs.

modules.name: aero_safety_controller
modules.description: Safety FSM and actuator command formatter supervising enable, freshness, timeout, heartbeat, clamping, fallback, and validated command issuance. Drives the bounded actuator outputs and IRQ signaling based on deterministic safety policy.
modules.functionality: Implements the FSM states RESET, SAFE_FALLBACK, READY, REQUESTED, WAIT_RESPONSE, APPLY_VALIDATED, and FAULT. Validates response freshness, age, timeout, and sequence matching; clamps actuator commands to the programmed bounds; forces safe fallback when conditions are invalid or firmware heartbeat is absent; and provides bounded-latency command outputs and fault interrupts.
responsibilities: Supervise the entire control loop safety policy.
Validate response matching and freshness.
Clamp positive and negative actuator channels independently.
Drive safe fallback outputs deterministically.
Assert IRQ on timeout, fault, stale data, invalid response, or watchdog expiry.
Encode the current mode and fault bits for firmware reads.
modules.reset_behavior: Enter SAFE_FALLBACK on reset, clear transient faults only per controlled clear-fault sequencing, and drive deterministic safe actuator outputs until a valid enabled state is re-established.
behavior_rules: act_valid shall assert only for validated, current, in-range commands.
act_safe shall indicate safe-state drive whenever fallback is active.
A stale or mismatched response shall not be applied to actuator outputs.
Timeouts and watchdog expiries shall force safe fallback and fault signaling.
Clamp-active shall reflect any saturation of act_pos or act_neg against configured bounds.
Sequence and age provenance must be preserved in the status outputs for verification.

modules.name: fpga_bram_reqresp_fifo_wrapper
modules.description: Technology-neutral FPGA BRAM wrapper for compact request/response FIFO storage. This instantiated child wrapper provides the read data producer and is mapped to the memory macro declared in memory_macros.
modules.functionality: Provides the instantiated FIFO BRAM interface for request and response transport staging. The wrapper exists so the memory macro is represented as a real hierarchy module rather than metadata only.
responsibilities: Expose the exact FPGA BRAM interface pins for the transport FIFO.
Map the technology-neutral wrapper to the declared memory macro.
Provide the FIFO read-data input to the transport block.
Keep storage implementation localized to block RAM semantics.
modules.reset_behavior: Hold control pins in an idle-safe state on reset and preserve memory contents as implementation-defined until rewritten.
behavior_rules: Must represent a real instantiated memory wrapper in the hierarchy.
Must not be flattened into registers or widened into a streaming bus.
The dout input is the producer-side read data interface observed by the transport block.

modules.name: fpga_bram_history_wrapper
modules.description: Technology-neutral FPGA BRAM wrapper for compact response history storage. This instantiated child wrapper provides history read-data to the transport block and is mapped to the memory macro declared in memory_macros.
modules.functionality: Provides the instantiated history BRAM interface for bounded storage of compact sequence and summary history. The wrapper exists so the memory macro is represented as a real hierarchy module rather than metadata only.
responsibilities: Expose the exact FPGA BRAM interface pins for response history.
Map the technology-neutral wrapper to the declared memory macro.
Provide the history read-data input to the transport block.
Keep storage implementation localized to block RAM semantics.
modules.reset_behavior: Hold control pins in an idle-safe state on reset and preserve memory contents as implementation-defined until rewritten.
behavior_rules: Must represent a real instantiated memory wrapper in the hierarchy.
Must not be flattened into registers or widened into a streaming bus.
The dout input is the producer-side read data interface observed by the transport block.
